title: Designing a Comprehensive Machine Learning-driven Prescriptive Clinical Decision Support System for Shock and Associated Critical Care Conditions
text:
Machine learning-driven complex decision making to manage shock and other critical care conditions are challenging with
its resource-intensive development pipeline and conflicting decisions. Our goal is to navigate this process with leveraging
multimodal foundation modeling to gain efficiency, creating a priority engine to streamline complex decisions, and safely
simulating this in data stream through silent deployment.

title: Research and Methods Core - Telehealth Research and Innovation for Veterans with Cancer (THRIVE)
text: The Veterans Affairs Health Administration (VA) is the largest integrated health care system in the US, caring for nearly 50,000 veterans with newly diagnosed cancer annually. Providing quality care for all veterans is a tenet of the VA healthcare mission. We hypothesize that there are factors (e.g., rurality, race/ethnicity and poverty) that are critical in determining access to healthcare, especially telehealth. Approximately 25% of veterans live in rural areas where there may not be adequate local VA cancer care facilities. Unfortunately, these same communities often lack specialized community-based cancer care services as well, making telehealth a necessary option to reduce barriers to quality, timely cancer care. However, little is known about how telehealth delivery for veterans with cancer impacts delivery of quality care, clinical outcomes and experiences of care. As a national integrated health care system focused on quality of cancer care, VA provides an outstanding national laboratory to examine how use of telehealth affects access and quality of care. We will be able to examine how interventions targeting specific factors such as rurality affect the use of telehealth and how use of telehealth affects quality. We will disseminate this information broadly to help other health care systems understand how best to integrate telehealth into the continuum of cancer care. Using principles of implementation science, Telehealth Research and Innovation for Veterans with Cancer (THRIVE) will build a new model of cancer care delivery addressing barriers to telehealth and fulfilling the promise of access to excellent cancer care for Veterans regardless of who they are or where they are located. The Research and Methods Core primarily focuses on understanding how to improve access to and quality of care for all Veterans. Our multidisciplinary team will achieve THRIVE’s vision by focusing on lung, colorectal, prostate and breast cancers and accomplishing five specific aims: (1) Assess stakeholders’ perspectives of contextual factors impacting cancer telehealth implementation and sustainment at multiple levels; (2) Measure the use of in- person and telehealth communication formats for cancer care throughout VA; (3) Evaluate what factors affect use of telehealth for cancer care and how telehealth use is associated with cancer care quality; (4) Oversee the selection, development, implementation and evaluation of 10 rapid-cycle pilot studies (2/year) at the intersection of implementation science and telehealth cancer care; and (5) Frame the affordability of scaling up effective interventions that are identified from the pilot studies.

title: Intraoperative fluorescence lifetime navigation system with deformation compensation and MRI/CT co-registration for precision imaging of oral cancer
text:
Cancer surgery currently relies mainly on the surgeon’s touch and feel to identify tumors during a surgery,
which can often lead tumors left behind and the recurrence of disease, or to the removal of too much healthy
tissue, which can affect normal functions such as speech. We will develop and test an imaging technique that
utilizes a safe FDA approved dye to enhance tumor brightness and provide a clear view of the surgical site and
vital organs. With this imaging technology, surgeons would be able to accurately localize and remove tumors,
while maximally preserving essential functions such as speech and swallowing.

title: AAV therapies for TNNT2-associated cardiac disorders
text:
Pathogenic variants in the cardiac troponin T gene (TNNT2) cause hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathies,
two disorders that are associated with high rates of heart failure and premature death unless new disease-
modifying therapies are developed. Our study will develop an adeno-associated virus therapy that replaces
pathogenic TNNT2 with its normal wildtype version by performing efficacy and safety screening in human
cardiomyocytes, 3-dimensional microtissues, and genetic mouse models. This research has the potential to
discover not only a new therapeutic for cardiomyopathy caused by TNNT2 variants, but a roadmap to develop
similar therapies for related genetic forms of heart failure.

title: Multimodal Molecular Imaging of Choroidal Neovascularization
text:
This project optimizes a new, safe imaging technology using a combination of light and sound in
large animal eye models of wet macular degeneration. Imaging characteristics predicting lack of
response to treatment are determined, and new nanoparticles for enhancement of imaging which
are able to be safely excreted in the urine are evaluated. The long term goal of this project is to
develop a multimodal molecular imaging using gold nanoparticles to image biomarkers predicting
response to treatment to develop novel therapies of eye diseases.

title: Mechanisms of nonvesicular cholesterol transport
text:
We have identified proteins that transfer cholesterol between different membranes in cells. We will define
molecular mechanisms whereby these proteins act, including identifying novel proteins with which they
cooperate to accomplish cholesterol movement. These studies are expected to provide fundamental insight
into pathways regulating cholesterol homeostasis and may suggest opportunities for modulating lipid levels
and metabolism.

title: Off-the-Shelf ADC-Armed NK Cells Platform for Multi-Indication Immunotherapy
text:
TO PUBLIC HEALTH
This project will develop a new type of cell-based therapy by combining natural killer cells with antibody-drug
conjugates, creating a flexible “off-the-shelf” treatment that can be cryopreserved and used for many different
diseases.

title: Studying the Utility of Deep Learning Derived MRI Imaging Biomarkers for Localized Prostate Cancer
text:
Prostate cancer remains a significant public health concern and remains the second leading cause of cancer
death among men in the United States. MRI biomarkers represent a promising strategy to aid in risk
stratification and treatment selection for localized prostate cancer patients. In this proposal, we attempt to
validate and implement novel MRI biomarkers, which can risk stratify and directly aid in treatment selection for
localized prostate cancer.

title: Membrane proteins driving a cell-cell fusion reaction during fertilization
text:
This project will use fertilization in the alga Chlamydomonas to uncover conserved mechanisms of cell-
cell fusion during fertilization, an event in the life of all eukaryotes which remains poorly understood. I
will focus on uncovering new mechanisms of regulation of the fusion protein HAP2, which is essential
for fertilization in unicellular and multicellular plants and animals, and that is in the same family of
proteins used by viruses to enter human cells. Because HAP2 is essential for sexual reproduction in the
malaria organism, Plasmodium, our findings will continue to advance strategies we have already
discovered for development of a transmission-blocking malaria vaccine.

title: Fibronectin Enriched Protein Corona for Enhanced Tumor Targeting of Nanoparticles
text:
Many cancer patients do not benefit from current nanomedicines because the nanoparticles fail to reach tumors
in sufficient amounts. This project will explore how naturally formed protein layers, called fibronectin-enriched
coronas, help nanoparticles cross blood vessel barriers, penetrate deeply into tumors, and deliver their
therapeutic payloads more effectively. By uncovering how nanoparticle design shapes corona formation and
tumor targeting, this work aims to develop simpler, ligand-free drug delivery systems that enhance selectivity
and efficiency of drug delivery to the tumors.

title: Systematic characterization of human disease associated protein complexes
text:
Protein complexes carry out nearly all biological functions in human cells and when disrupted
they give rise to many diseases including cancer, developmental disorders, and cardiovascular
disease. Currently, we lack understanding of the composition of many protein complexes. Using
mass spectrometry based experiments and sophisticated computer algorithms (e.g. machine
learning/AI), I propose to 1) discover new protein complex variants, 2) understand how protein
complexes are altered in different cell types, and 3) create three dimensional models of protein
complexes to interpret disease mutations, possibly opening new avenues for therapeutic
interventions.

title: Identifying mechanisms of structural variant-induced gene activation in glioma
text:
Gliomas are a class of primary brain tumors with historically poor prognosis and very few novel treatment options.
The aggressive nature of this cancer, which virtually always results in fatal recurrence, can be attributed in part
to its clonal and genetic heterogeneity which includes chromosomal aberrations. This proposal explores the
landscape of structural variants in patient gliomas and seeks to define the mechanism by which these large-
scale mutations are regulated and how they contribute to disease progression.

title: North American Testis Workshop 2026
text:
This R13 application requests funds to support the XXVIIIth North American Testis Workshop to
be held from April 15-18, 2026, at the Embassy Suites by Hilton Scottsdale Resort in Scottsdale,
Arizona. The meeting will bring together leading experts, emerging scientists, and trainees
working in the field of testis biology from North America and around the world. Participants will
share and discuss their latest data and technologies that could translate into new opportunities
for resolving important medical and public health issues.

title: Origins and Outcomes of Smartphone and Social Media Habits Across Development
text:
The emergence of new technology/media forms has often been accompanied by panic over the likely societal
and personal harms they might engender, especially with respect to developing youth. The proposed project
seeks to inform our understanding of the particular precursors, correlates, and sequelae that may be linked to
the escalating presence of smartphone and social media technologies in teens' lives, and to guide us in
determining when these technology habits should, and should not, concern policy-makers and care-givers. The
project will enact a multi-methodological cross-sequential longitudinal study to investigate the psychological
and brain factors that predispose individuals of different ages to intensified use of smartphones and social
media (SSM), and to explore the relationship that such habits may have with specific aspects of cognitive and
brain development, psychosocial maturation, and everyday functioning.

title: IND-enabling studies of non-immunogenic gene therapy for ultra-rare DMD patients excluded from dystrophin trials
text:
This proposal is focused on translational and clinical research in gene therapy to safely address an ultra-rare
subset of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients excluded from ongoing dystrophin-based gene
therapy trials. The rationale is the avoidance of destructive T cell responses to dystrophin epitopes by
substituting the non-immunogenic dystrophin-related protein utrophin, composed entirely of “self” peptide
epitopes to take advantage of central immunological tolerance. The project makes appropriate use of
preclinical models to address major limitations identified in ongoing clinical studies, focusing on IND-enabling
experiments that pertain to both FDA regulations and to the anticipated risks and potential benefits to DMD
patients.

title: Using Glycomic Signatures to Monitor Disease Progression and Predict Treatment Response in Lupus Nephritis
text:
Lupus Nephritis, a severe kidney disease impacting nearly half of all lupus patients, often leads to unfavorable
patient outcomes. Existing biomarkers such as the urinary protein/creatinine ratio (UPrUCr) fall short in
accurately gauging treatment response, requiring repeating biopsies to monitor disease progression. The goal
of this proposal is to assess the predictive potential of glycomic signatures (N-glycosylated proteins) present in
the urine of patients with lupus nephritis, offering a more sensitive and less invasive alternative ultimately
enhancing current clinical methods and improving patient outcomes.

title: Phenotypic marker-guided development of selective antimetastasis therapeutic leads
text:
The lack of effective treatment against metastatic cancer is primarily due to the complexity of the disease and
incomplete understanding of the key mechanisms. We address this challenge through an unconventional
approach that takes advantage of a specific feature of cancer cells distinguishing them from normal cells. We
use this unique feature to develop anti-cancer drugs for discovery of agents selective against cancer cells over
normal cells. We have developed a clinical candidate (metarrestin) that shows selective inhibition of cancer
metastasis in animals. Metarrestin has begun a phase I pancreatic cancer clinical trial at NCI. We will investigate
how this compound inhibits cancer behavior and will develop next generation, more specific and potent anti-
cancer drugs.

title: Mechanisms of Incomplete Penetrance
text:
Diseases attributable to mutations in a single gene effect an estimated 1 in 100 people,
however, many of these diseases display incomplete penetrance. Incomplete
penetrance is a phenomenon in which some individuals with a known disease-causing
mutation develop disease symptoms, while others do not. Understanding the biological
mechanisms by which some individuals are resilient to their genetic mutations will
provide new avenues for developing treatments for genetic disorders.

title: Protein Degradation Strategies to Overcome Menin Drug Resistance in Acute Leukemias
text:
MENIN, a nuclear protein that plays several roles in gene regulation, is crucial for the development of acute
leukemias in patients with MLL1 (KMT2A) gene rearrangements (MLLr). MLLrs occur in ~10% of adult acute
myeloid leukemia (AML) and acute lymphocytic leukemias (ALL) cases and ~80% of infant leukemia cases; the
5-year survival rate for MLLr leukemias overall is a dismal 35%. Using structure-based drug design, we have
devised, and will evaluate, molecules that can accomplish sustained and irreversible inhibition of the MENIN–
MLL protein–protein interaction (PPI) that is foundational in this undrugged mechanism of leukemia
development, biology and progression to drug resistance; crucially our strategy of degrading the MENIN
protein is designed to overcome resistance observed with existing MENIN inhibitor clinical candidates.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Biodosimetry for High-Throughput Radiation Triage via Chromosomal Aberration Detection
text:
Advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning (DL) have the potential to transform radiation
biodosimetry by detecting a broader range of complex chromosomal aberrations beyond dicentric chromosomes.
This approach can accommodate diverse radiation exposures, including photons, neutrons, and mixed sources.
By enabling faster and more comprehensive categorization of radiation doses, these innovations can improve
triage systems, creating more precise exposure categories that enhance decision-making and response
capabilities during large-scale radiological events.
